1.explanation: The Dart highlighter registers two comment patterns in this order: first a doc-comment mode (hljs.COMMENT('/**', '*/')) and then the generic C-style block comment mode (hljs.C_BLOCK_COMMENT_MODE). The doc-comment begin pattern '/**' also matches the start of an empty comment '/**/'. As a result, the empty comment is consumed by the doc-comment rule, and because it wraps a zero-length payload, the highlighter never drops back into normal code mode. This prevents subsequent tokens (like identifiers and braces) from being recognized and highlighted. To fix it, the doc-comment rule should be adjusted (for example by requiring at least one non-slash character inside) or reordered so that empty comments are handled by the generic C_BLOCK_COMMENT_MODE and do not disrupt the normal parsing flow.

2.explanation: The broken highlighting traces back to the Dart language definition in src/languages/dart.js. The module’s exported function installs two comment modes for /**…*/ and generic /*…*/. The empty doc-comment mode (hljs.COMMENT('/**','*/',…)) matches /**/ but immediately closes, which disrupts the internal parser state and prevents subsequent tokens from being processed. The fallback C_BLOCK_COMMENT_MODE also overlaps this pattern but is never reached in the empty-comment case. Fixing or reordering these comment definitions in the exported function will restore proper tokenization after /**/.
2.bug_scenario: When a Dart source snippet begins and ends with an empty block comment (/**/main(){…}/**/), the highlighter consumes the empty comment in such a way that no further Dart tokens (keywords, punctuation, etc.) are highlighted after that comment. Instead of seeing “main” in keyword or function-name styling and the parentheses, strings, etc., all the remaining text is rendered as plain text.
